arguments: {"test_id": "T2", "per_hypothesis": [{"id": "H1", "verdict": "weakened", "why": "The interface arm, which is the only T2 measurement that bears on H1, returned no predicted protein-protein interface containing residue 28 (ProtVar interface state not_covered, in_predicted_interface false). This is a weak negative: the test used the monomer AF-Q06187-F1 model, so it cannot see a PH-TH dimer, and not_covered means the tool could not evaluate the interface. Support from E9 and E11 is unchanged."}, {"id": "H2", "verdict": "supported", "why": "Residue 28 falls in ProtVar predicted pocket 8 (score 889.4, buriedness 0.8, mean pLDDT of pocket residues 86.3), the pocket type that the test scored as weak support for H2. It is absent from all 13 P2Rank pockets, so the support is weak and model-dependent. H2's refute criterion (no ligand-phosphate proximity in 1B55 or other IP-bound entries) is not met by T2."}, {"id": "H3", "verdict": "unchanged", "why": "T2 measures pockets and interfaces, not folding stability, so it does not bear on the R28H stability claim. T3 is the test for H3."}], "uncertainty": "T2 uses predicted pockets and interfaces on a single AlphaFold monomer model, so neither arm measures a binding site or a dimer. The pocket hit and P2Rank miss disagree, and the interface result is not_covered, so H1 is only weakened and H2 only weakly supported. Controls: pocket rank and pLDDT were reported (pocket 8, pLDDT 86.3), but the test did not run negative-control residues for the pocket arm, and the interface control is unavailable. No experimental binding or dimer measurement of R28H is available. Validation still needed: an R28H-specific IP4 binding measurement and a dimer-interface model or assay."}

name: record_decision
arguments: {"favoured_after": "H2", "why": "Previous favourite H2 (inositol-phosphate pocket) is kept. Its direct support is E6 (UniProt binding site at residue 28 for Ins(1,3,4,5,)P4, PubMed 10196129), E17 (1B55 with IP4), E13 and E15 (MD and MM/PBSA on R28C/H, literature), plus T1 (ligand contact in 32 of 39 structures, 4IP at 2.75 \u00c5 in 1BWN, and negative-control ligands never contacting the residue). T2 (test T2) adds a weak pocket hit for H2 (ProtVar pocket 8, pLDDT 86.3) that is missed by P2Rank. Strongest rival H1 (PH-TH dimer disruption) has direct support in E9 (this exact substitution, reported impaired activation via prevented dimerisation), with E11 inferential because it studies E41K. T2 takes away from H1: no predicted interface contains residue 28 (not_covered, monomer model). H1 is weakened but not refuted, since its refute criterion needs a dimer model that T2 did not run. H2 remains better supported than H1, so the favourite is unchanged. Evidence: E6, E9, E11, E13, E15, E17, E19, E20, E21, T1, T2."}

name: record_next_experiment
arguments: {"description": "R28H-specific ligand-binding check on the 1B55 PH domain with IP4 bound: model the R28H substitution in the IP4-bound structure, then compare the contacts and MM/PBSA binding free energy against the wild-type. Also count partner-protomer contacts in a PH-TH dimer model built from 1B55 and the E41K dimer to test H1. H2 is refuted if residue 28 has no phosphate-oxygen contact within 4 \u00c5 and R28H binding energy matches wild-type within MM/PBSA error. H1 is refuted if no atom of residue 28 lies within 5 \u00c5 of the partner protomer and the interface contacts are unchanged by R28H.", "kind": "computational", "why_now": "H2 is favoured by a small margin, and its key claim (R28H reduces IP4 binding) has not been measured for this substitution. The T2 pocket result is weak and model-dependent. A wild-type versus R28H comparison on the IP4-bound structure directly tests H2's refute criterion and can be run cheaply, while the dimer check tests the strongest rival H1. Both outcomes change the ranking."}
